text:
In the formula $X = 5YZ^{2}$
, X and Z have dimensions of capacitance and magnetic field, respectively. What are
the dimensions of Y in SI units?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Capacitance (C) = $\frac{Q^{2}}{2E}$ = $\frac{\left [A^{2}T^{2}\right ]}{[ML^{2}T^{-2}]}$ = $\left [M^{-1}L^{-2}T^{4}A^{2}\right ]$ X

Magnetic field (B) = $\frac{F}{IL}$ = $\frac{\left [MLT^{-2}\right ]}{[A][L]}$ = $\left [MT^{-2}A^{-1}\right ]$ = Z

Given,

$X = 5YZ^{2}$

$\therefore$ Y = $\frac{X}{5Z^{2}}$

[Y] = $\frac{\left [M^{-1}L^{-2}T^{4}A^{2}\right ]}{[MT^{-2}A^{-1}]^{2}}$

$\therefore$ [Y] =  [$M^{–3}L^{–2}T^{8}A^{4}$]
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot

text:
In free space, a particle A of charge 1$μ$C is held fixed at a point P. Another particle B of the same charge and
mass 4$μ$g is kept at a distance of 1 mm from P. If B is released, then its velocity at a distance of 9 mm from P
is :
$\left [Take\frac{1}{4π\in _{0}}=9\times 10^{9}Nm^{2}C^{-2}\right ]$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$q_{A} = 1$ $μ$C ; $q_{B} = 1$ $μC, m_{B} = 4 × 10^{–9} kg, r_{AB} = 10^{–3} m$

$\frac{1}{2}M_{B}V^{2}=kq_{A}q_{B}\left \{\frac{1}{10^{-3}}-\frac{1}{9\times 10^{-3}}\right \}$

$\frac{1}{2}4\times 10^{-9}V^{2}=9\times 10^{9}\times 10^{-12}\times \frac{8}{9}\times 10^{3}$

$V^{2}=\frac{8}{2}\times 10^{9}=4\times 10^{9}$

V =  $\sqrt{40}\times 10^{4}m/s$ = 6.32 $\times$ $10^{4} m/s$

Note: In the original JEE Main paper the options were 1.0 m/s, 1.5 $\times$ $10^{2} m/s, 2.0$ $\times$ $10^{3} m/s$ and 3.0 $\times$ $10^{4} m/s$, and NTA's key was 2.0 $\times$ $10^{3} m/s$, which corresponds to a mass of $4 mg (4 × 10^{–6} kg)$. For the mass printed in the question, 4 $μg = 4 × 10^{–9} kg$, the speed is 6.32 $\times$ $10^{4} m/s ($option B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot

text:
A bullet of mass 20 g has an initial speed of $1 ms^{–1}$
, just before it starts penetrating a mud wall of thickness
20 cm. If the wall offers a mean resistance of $2.5 × 10^{–2} N$, the speed of the bullet after emerging from the
other side of the wall is close to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, resistance offered by the wall

$=F=-2.5\times 10^{-2}\mathrm{N}$

So, deacceleration of bullet,

$\left. \begin{array}{ll} a=\dfrac{F}{m}=\dfrac{-2.5\times 10^{-2}}{20\times 10^{-3}} & =-\dfrac{5}{4}\mathrm{ms}^{-2} \\  \\ (\because m & =20\mathrm{g}=20\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{kg}\right ) \end{array}$

Now, using the equation of motion,

$v^{2}-u^{2}=2as$

We have,

$v^{2}=1+2\left (-\frac{5}{4}\right )\left (20\times 10^{-2}\right )$

$\left (\because u=1\mathrm{ms}^{-1}\text{and}s=20\mathrm{cm}=20\times 10^{-2}\mathrm{m}\right )$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow v^{2}=\frac{1}{2} \\  \\ \therefore v=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\approx 0.7\mathrm{ms}^{-1} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot

text:
One mole of ideal gas passes through a process where pressure and volume obey the relation
$P=P_{0}\left [1-\frac{1}{2}\left (\frac{V_{0}}{V}\right )^{2}\right ]$.
Here $P_{0}$ and $V_{0}$ are constants. Calculate the change in the temperature of the gas if its
volume changes form $V_{0}$ to $2V_{0}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given $P=P_{o}\left \{1-\frac{1}{2}\left (\frac{V_{o}}{V}\right )^{2}\right \};$ ...(i)

As n = 1 mole

$\therefore$ PV = nRT = RT

$\Rightarrow$ P = $\frac{RT}{V}$ ....(ii)

From (i) and (ii), we get

$\frac{RT}{V}=P_{0}\left [1-\frac{1}{2}\left (\frac{V_{0}}{V}\right )^{2}\right ]$

$\Rightarrow$ T = $\frac{V}{R}\times P_{0}\left [1-\frac{1}{2}\left (\frac{V_{0}}{V}\right )^{2}\right ]$

Case 1 : when $V = V_{0}$

then $T_{i} =$ $\frac{V_{0}}{R}\times P_{0}\left [1-\frac{1}{2}\left (\frac{V_{0}}{V_{0}}\right )^{2}\right ]$

= $\frac{V_{0}P_{0}}{2R}$

Case 2 : when $V = 2V_{0}$

then $T_{f} =$ $\frac{2V_{0}}{R}\times P_{0}\left [1-\frac{1}{2}\left (\frac{V_{0}}{2V_{0}}\right )^{2}\right ]$

= $\frac{7}{4}\frac{P_{0}V_{0}}{R}$

Then $\DeltaT = T_{f} - T_{i}$

= $\frac{7}{4}\frac{P_{0}V_{0}}{R}-\frac{P_{0}V_{0}}{2R}$

= $\frac{P_{0}V_{0}}{R}\left (\frac{7}{4}-\frac{1}{2}\right )$

= $\frac{5}{4}\frac{P_{0}V_{0}}{R}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot

text:
Water from a tap emerges vertically downwards with an initial speed of $1.0 ms^{–1}$
. The cross-sectional area of
the tap is $10^{–4} m^{2}$. Assume that the pressure is constant throughout the stream of water and that the flow is streamlined. The cross-sectional area of the stream, 0.15 m below the tap would be : (Take $g = 10 ms^{–2})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
With the pressure constant along the stream, Bernoulli's equation reduces to free fall, so the speed $0.15$ m below the tap is

$v_{2}=\sqrt{v_{1}^{2}+2gh}=\sqrt{1^{2}+2\times 10\times 0.15}=\sqrt{4}=2\text{m s}^{-1}$

By the equation of continuity, $A_{1}v_{1}=A_{2}v_{2}$:

$A_{2}=\dfrac{A_{1}v_{1}}{v_{2}}=\dfrac{10^{-4}\times 1}{2}=5\times 10^{-5}\text{m}^{2}$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot

text:
A square loop is carrying a steady current I and the magnitude of its magnetic dipole moment is m. if this
square loop is changed to a circular loop and it carries the same current, the magnitude of the magnetic dipole
moment of circular loop will be:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the given square loop has side $a$, then its magnetic dipole moment will be

$m=Ia^{2}$

When square is converted into a circular loop of radius $r$,


[IMG]


Then, wire length will be same in both area,

$\Rightarrow 4a=2πr\Rightarrow r=\frac{4a}{2π}=\frac{2a}{π}$

Hence, area of circular loop formed is, $A^{'}=πr^{2}$

$=π\left (\frac{2a}{π}\right )^{2}=\frac{4a^{2}}{π}$

Magnitude of magnetic dipole moment of circular loop will be

$m^{'}=IA^{'}=I\frac{4a^{2}}{π}$

Ratio of magnetic dipole moments of both shapes is,

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{m^{'}}{m}=\dfrac{I\cdot \frac{4a^{2}}{π}}{Ia^{2}}=\dfrac{4}{π} \\  \\ \Rightarrow m^{'}=\dfrac{4m}{π}(\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{m}) \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot

text:
A submarine experiences a pressure of $5.05 × 10^{6}$
 Pa at a depth of $d_{1}$ in a sea. When it goes further to a depth
of $d_{2}$, it experiences a pressure of $8.08 × 10^{6}$
 Pa. Then $d_{2} –d_{1}$ is approximately (density of water $= 10^{3}$
 $kg/m^{3}$
and acceleration due to gravity $= 10 ms^{–2}$
) :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The pressure experienced by a submarine at a certain depth in the sea is given by the formula:

$P=ρgh$

where:

$P$ is the pressure
$ρ$ is the density of the fluid (sea water in this case)
$g$ is the acceleration due to gravity
$h$ is the height (or depth in this case)

Given:

$ρ=10^{3}kg/m^{3}$
$g=10m/s^{2}$

We are looking for the difference in depth, $d_{2}-d_{1}$, which corresponds to the difference in pressure $\Delta P$:

$\Delta P=P_{2}-P_{1}=ρg(d_{2}-d_{1})$

Rearranging the above equation, we get:

$d_{2}-d_{1}=\frac{\Delta P}{ρg}$

Given:

$P_{2}=8.08\times 10^{6}Pa$
$P_{1}=5.05\times 10^{6}Pa$

$\Delta P=P_{2}-P_{1}=8.08\times 10^{6}Pa-5.05\times 10^{6}Pa=3.03\times 10^{6}Pa$

So, 

$d_{2}-d_{1}=\frac{3.03\times 10^{6}Pa}{10^{3}kg/m^{3}\times 10m/s^{2}}=303m$

The closest answer among the options provided is Option C, 300 m.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot

$/kg^{2}$]

The magnitude of the magnetic field at the centre of an equilateral triangular loop of side 1 m which is

 $NA^{–2}$]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a current carrying wire, magnetic field at
a distance r is given by


[IMG]


$B=\frac{μ_{0}i}{4πr}(\sin θ_{1}+\sin θ_{2})$

Now, in given case,


[IMG]


Due to symmetry of arrangement, net field at centre of triangle is

$\begin{array}{ll} B_{\text{net}} & =\text{Sum of fields of all wires (sides)} \\  \\ =3\times \dfrac{μ_{0}i}{4πr}(\sin θ_{1}+\sin θ_{2}) \end{array}$

Here, $θ_{1}=θ_{2}=60^{\circ }$

$\begin{array}{l} \therefore \sin θ_{1}=\sin θ_{2}=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2},i=10\mathrm{A},\dfrac{μ_{0}}{4π}=10^{-7}\mathrm{NA}^{-2} \\  \\ \text{and}r=\dfrac{1}{3}\times \text{altitude} \\  \\ =\dfrac{1}{3}\times \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\times \text{sides length}=\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{3}}\times 1\mathrm{m}=\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{3}}\mathrm{m} \end{array}$

So,

$\begin{array}{ll} B_{\mathrm{net}} & =\dfrac{3\times 10^{-7}\times 10\times 2\left (\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right )}{\left (\frac{1}{2\sqrt{3}}\right )}=18\times 10^{-6}\mathrm{T} \\  \\ \Rightarrow B_{\mathrm{net}} & =18μ\mathrm{T} \end{array}$

text:
A plane is inclined at an angle $α$ = 30° with respect to the horizontal. A particle is projected with a speed u =
$2 ms^{–1}$
, from the base of the plane, making an angle $θ$ = 15° with respect to the plane as shown in the figure.
The distance from the base, at which the particle hits the plane is close to : 
(Take g = 10 ms
$^{–2})$

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$T=\frac{2u\sin θ}{g\cos α}$

$R=u\cos θT-\frac{1}{2}g\sin αT^{2}$

$=\frac{u\cos θ2u\sin θ}{g\cos α}-\frac{g\sin α}{2}\frac{4u^{2}\sin ^{2}θ}{g^{2}\cos ^{2}α}$

$=\frac{u^{2}\sin 2θ}{g\cos α}-\frac{u^{2}\sin α}{g\cos ^{2}α}\{1-\cos 2θ\}$

$=\frac{4\times \frac{1}{2}}{10\times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}-\frac{u^{2}\sin α}{g\cos ^{2}α}\left \{1-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right \}$

$=\frac{4}{10\sqrt{3}}-\frac{8}{30}\left \{1-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right \}$

$=\frac{4}{5\sqrt{3}}-\frac{8}{30}=\frac{8\sqrt{3}-8}{30}$

$=\frac{8\left (\sqrt{3}-1\right )}{30}=20cm$

text:
The graph shows how the magnification m produced by a thin lens varies with image distance v. What is the focal length of the lens used?

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
As the graph between magnification (m) and
image distance (v) varies linearly, then

$m = k_{1}v + k_{2}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{v}{u}=k_{1}v+k_{2}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{u}=k_{1}+\frac{k_{2}}{v}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{k_{2}}{v}-\frac{1}{u}=k_{1}$

Clearly, $k_{1}=\frac{1}{f}$ and  $k_{2} = 1$ here

$\therefore f=\frac{1}{slopeofm-ygraph}=\frac{b}{c}$

A cubical block of side 0.5 m floats on water with 30% of its volume under water. What is the maximum
weight that can be put on the block without fully submerging it under water? [Take, density of water $= 10^{3}$
$kg/m^{3}$]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given $(50)^{3}\times \frac{30}{100}\times (1)\times g=M_{cube}g$    ...(i)

Let m mass should be placed

Hence $(50)^{3}\times$ (1) $\times$ $g =  (M_{$cube} + m)g   …(ii)

equation (ii) – equation (i)

$\Rightarrow$ $mg = (50)^{3} × g(1 – 0.3) = 125 × 0.7 × 10^{3} g$

$\Rightarrow$ m = 87.5 kg

text:
A 2 mW laser operates at wavelength of 500 nm. The number of photons that will be emitted per second is :
[Given Planck's constant $h = 6.6 × 10^{–34} Js$, speed of light $c = 3.0 × 10^{8}$
 m/s]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$2\times 10^{-3}=\frac{hc}{λ}\frac{dn}{dt}$

$\frac{dn}{dt}=\frac{2\times 10^{-3}λ}{hc}$

$=\frac{2\times 10^{-3}\times 500\times 10^{-9}}{6.6\times 10^{-34}\times 3\times 10^{8}}$

$=\frac{1000}{6.6\times 3}\times 10=5\times 10^{15}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot

text:
When heat Q is supplied to a diatomic gas of rigid molecules, at constant volume its temperature increases by
$\Delta$T. the heat required to produce the same change in temperature, at a constant pressure is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Heat supplied at constant volume

$Q = nC_{V}\Delta$T

and heat supplied at constant pressure

$Q' = nC_{P}\Delta$T

$Q^{'}=\frac{C_{P}}{C_{V}}Q=\left (1+\frac{2}{5}\right )Q=\frac{7}{5}Q$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot
